_comment: Unattended reviews held for the owner. Both plugins must give the agent `held_text`, and the owner each notice's `text` with {allow}, {deny} and {why} replaced by their commands (/sentrook allow, /sentrook deny and /sentrook why on Hermes, /sentrook-allow, /sentrook-deny and /sentrook-why on OpenClaw). `where` is built from its parts as `where_text`. `offers` are the answers the hold offers, in the notice's order, from the run's cron job (`where.job_id`), the response's `owner_pass` (absent, as from a scanner that predates it, null or any other value: no pass; and no pass at all for a scan that is enforced, has a floor or is not complete, since no pass could let it through), whether the call names its parties (the entities its reasons and description name, with an approval fingerprint that names something) and its risk against `block_at`: on a cron job `allow` when there is a level, then `allow later` (or `allow now` when the held run had already acted, `acted`: see `run_now`), `allow always` at level always for a named call below the block line, and `deny`; on another run with a source (`where.source`: its kind and the host's value, shown by name; see `sources`) the same without `allow later` or `allow now`, and with the answers' lines naming the source; elsewhere `allow` alone, bound to the exact call. Chat markup (`[]()<>|@` and backticks) is taken out of every field the agent can influence (job id and name, tool, target description), and the target description is capped at 160 characters. The notice never carries the risk, reason codes, scores, entity kinds or the suggested grant: Hermes copies what it sends into the agent's own transcript. A call a denial for its job settles gets `declined_text`. `passes` says when a pass set at `pass_level` from the `held` response lets a later call (`later`, with `later_tool` when the tool differs, and `args`/`later_args` for a call that names nothing) through: same tool, same parties, risk no higher, no new warning (every reason code but the scanner's scoring and wording notes), not enforced, no floor, a complete scan, and the later scan's owner_pass at or above the pass's level. `hints` lists suggested grants and what the grant command accepts (null: refused). `outcomes` says what each verdict becomes on an attended and an unattended run with review at 40 and block at 80: a block, from the line or enforced, is never held. `history` gives the action and review columns history prints for held scans and calls a pass or denial settled. An outcome's `ceiling` is the scanner's verdict ceiling; an unattended run never lowers a block to a review with it, so a lowered block is never held, except when the response's `reasons` include `cap.unanswered_retry` (a retry of a review nobody answered may ask, never block on its own) or `cap.local_code` (code that reaches no network sink may be reviewed or held, never blocked): that block is held. `scan_failure_notices` are the owner's notices when a scan failure blocks a call on an unattended run: the same shape, with {verify} replaced by the host's setup check (hermes sentrook verify, openclaw sentrook verify). There is no hold id: nothing is held. The reason names the failure kind (`reasons`), never its detail. After one is sent, further scan failures with the same `quiet_key` (the cron job id when known, else the session) send none for `scan_failure_quiet_hours`.
held_text: Sentrook held this tool call for the owner's approval, so it did not run. Do not retry this call in this run.
declined_text: The owner declined this action for this job, so Sentrook did not run it. Continue without it.

run_now._comment: Plain `allow` on a held call of a cron job sets a one-use pass bound to a new run of the job and starts that run now: Hermes runs `hermes cron run <job>` (Hermes's own `cron.jobs.trigger_job` in process when the launcher is not there), OpenClaw runs `openclaw cron run <job> --json`. On OpenClaw the pass is bound to the run id that command returns (the job's running receipt names it); on Hermes to the job's first run that starts after the answer, other than the held run. `allow <id> later` sets a pass for the job's next run and starts nothing. A run is started at most once per hold (the hold is answered). Nothing is started, and the pass waits for the job's next run, when a guard applies (`reasons`, checked in this order): observe mode, the job cannot be read, it is gone, finished, paused, running now (or a run the plugin started for an earlier answer has not ended yet), changed since the hold (a digest of its settings, not of its run state, kept on the hold from its first notice; a job unreadable then stays unknown), or the held run had already acted before the held call (`acted`) and the owner did not answer `allow <id> now`. A call acted when it ran with a tool kind in `acting_kinds` or a scan category in `acting_categories`. `replies` are the owner's replies with {job} the job id, {id} the hold, {pass} the pass, {until} its expiry, {passes} and {allow} the commands, {reason} one of `reasons`. When the triggered run ends, the owner gets one `outcomes` line ({job}, {hold} a hold the run made): `passed` when the call went through, `passed_held` when it also made a held call, `held` when it only made a held call, `none` otherwise (the pass was not what let a call through: the run did not make the call, or the scanner allowed, blocked or another answer settled it). A pass bound to a run that ended unused is dropped.

reasons.unknown: Sentrook could not read the job, so it cannot check that the job is unchanged since the hold
reasons.terminal: the job has finished and is not scheduled to run again
reasons.running: the job is running now, or a run started for an earlier answer has not finished
reasons.changed: the job was changed since the call was held
reasons.acted: the held run had already sent or written something before this call, and a new run would do it again
reasons.unavailable: Sentrook cannot start the job from here

replies.started: Running job {job} again now; this call will be let through once in that run. Undo: {passes} revoke {pass}.
replies.started_now: Running job {job} again now; this call will be let through once in that run. The whole job runs again, so what it already sent or wrote before this call happens again. Undo: {passes} revoke {pass}.
replies.later: Job {job} may make this call once, on its next scheduled run, until {until}. Sentrook does not run the held call itself. Undo: {passes} revoke {pass}.
replies.fallback: Job {job} may make this call once, on its next scheduled run, until {until}. It was not run again now: {reason}. Undo: {passes} revoke {pass}.

outcomes.passed: Sentrook: cron job {job} ran again, and the call you allowed went through once.
outcomes.passed_held: Sentrook: cron job {job} ran again, and the call you allowed went through once. It also made a different call, held as {hold}.
outcomes.held: Sentrook: cron job {job} ran again but did not make the call you allowed; it made a different call, held as {hold}.
outcomes.none: Sentrook: cron job {job} ran again without using your answer.

sources._comment: Unattended runs that are not cron jobs bind a hold's answers to where the run came from, as the host's run metadata names it (never the prompt or the call): a heartbeat's agent id, a webhook's hook or route name, a subagent's parent session ref, an API-server key's name. `refs` gives each source's ref: the kind's prefix and the first 12 hex digits of sha256("<kind>\n<value>"). On such a hold `allow` is a one-use pass for the next matching call from the same source within `exact_pass_days` (nothing is started), and `allow always` and `deny` are bound to the same source for `pass_days`; a call from another source of the same kind, or from no source, is held. A run with no source keeps `allow` alone, bound to the exact call. `replies` are the owner's replies to each answer with {subject} from `subjects`, {until} the pass's expiry, {passes} the passes command and {pass} its id. `passes_list` is how the passes list and the dashboard show a source's pass or denial, with {until} its expiry.

replies.allow: {subject} may make this call once more, until {until}. Sentrook does not run the held call itself. Undo: {passes} revoke {pass}.
replies.allow always: {subject} may make this call until {until}. Undo: {passes} revoke {pass}.
replies.deny: {subject} will not make this call until {until}; you won't be told again. Undo: {passes} revoke {pass}.

run_group._comment: One notice per cron run: the end line listing a run's other held calls, and the replies to allow <lead> all (both plugins).
run_group.head: Sentrook: the run of cron job {job} that held {lead} also held {n} other call(s); none of them ran:
run_group.own_answer: (it sends or writes: answer it on its own)
run_group.all: Let {lead} and the calls listed here through once, in one new run of the job: {allow} {lead} all
run_group.each: Or answer each by its id: {allow} <id>, {deny} <id>. For the reasons: {why} <id>
run_group.covered: In that run, these listed calls may also go through once: {ids}.
run_group.left: Not covered, answer each on its own: {ids}.
run_group.none_listed: No other call of this run has been listed yet, so this answers {lead} alone.
run_group.not_lead: {id} is one of the calls held in the run that {lead} leads: answer it on its own id, or all of them with {allow} {lead} all.

dismiss._comment: dismiss <id> or dismiss all (both plugins): takes waiting holds off the list as if they had expired now, on any hold, whatever answers it offers. The held call never runs and nothing is set: no pass, denial or grant, and the session history is left as an expiry leaves it; a later call like it is held again. Each held call gets a resolution record hold_dismissed. {dismiss} is the host's command (/sentrook-dismiss on OpenClaw, /sentrook dismiss on Hermes).
dismiss.one: Dismissed {id}: the held call does not run and nothing was set. A call like it is held again next time.
dismiss.all: Dismissed {n} held call(s): {ids}. None of them runs and nothing was set. Calls like them are held again next time.
dismiss.usage: usage: {dismiss} <id>|all, with the id from Sentrook's notice (h- and 6 hex digits)
